cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You told the trainees their head trainer was an idiot. I want an apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. For undermining their head trainer. They still need to follow my instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email them after tomorrow's drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read it to them before the drill. My whistle isn't going to outrank 'idiot' on its own.

mechanism: A dictates when and how an apology must restore the trainer position before the next exercise, using superior direction to pursue position-specific respect.
confusable: An apology for a failed drill is not enough; the Drive requires acknowledgment of undermining A role in front of the people expected to follow it.
comparison: Public trainees and next-day drill timing differ from the chair scene private correction of apology wording.
seedUse: The existing D51-b demand for before-drill public repair already joins S01 control with role-disrespect acknowledgment.
